summary: I checked the Brazil presidential election, which votes today, and the NFL injury reports for Sunday's games. Three major pollsters (AtlasIntel, Datafolha, Quaest) all show Lula leading the first-round vote count by 3 to 6 points over Flavio Bolsonaro, yet the market only prices Lula's chance of winning the first round at 62 cents, so I bought a small position on Lula to win the first round. The NFL injury news I found, including backup quarterbacks starting for Chicago and Tampa Bay, is all several days old and already reflected in the betting lines, so I made no NFL trades this cycle.

trades.reasoning: AtlasIntel (Sept 29, n=5005, MoE 1pt) has Lula at 45.3-46.2% vs Flavio 42.2-43.1%; Datafolha (Oct 1) has Lula 45% vs Flavio 40%; Quaest (Sept 28) has Lula 39% vs Flavio 34%. All three major pollsters agree Lula leads the first-round vote count by 3 to 6 points, but the market prices Lula to win the first round at only 62 cents, which undervalues that consistent lead even after discounting for Brazil's history of underestimating right-wing turnout.
